Prevention: Harvest grains early or promptly to avoid field infestation transfer into storage
Clean the storage facility thoroughly and burn all sweepings, stored cowpea should not be kept on a bare floor
Paint the storage facility or fill up all cracks and crevices to make insect pests easy to detect
Avoid the use of old storage bags and containers.
Otherwise clean bags and storage containers before filling grain
Ensure that grains are clean and dried to a safe moisture level of 8- 10 % before storage
Purdue tripple plastic bags for storage
Monitoring: Additional relevant crops: groundnuts, french beans, pigeon pea, mung beans
Monitor 2-3 weeks after storage of grains.
Larvae (which are responsible for major damage) are small, white, C-shaped worms
Look in grains for adult beetles or cream coloured eggs or exit holes on grains
Look for powder or dust in the bag.
This is the crumbs created by the larvae feeding on the grains
If inspection reveals at least 3 infested grains or 1 adult beetles per 2kg of sample, initiate direct control
Direct Control: Remove grains from store and sun dry for at least 3 days to kill adults and developing larvae
Mix 5 ml of groundnut oil to 1 kg of cowpea grains and store in air-tight containers (for short-time storage and small quantities of grains)
Add 1500 g of dried chilli to one bag of dried cowpea grains (for long-time storage)
Mix seeds with non-toxic chemicals such as vegetable oils or neem ( Azadirachta indica ) seed extracts (e.g. 0.03 % Nimbedicine
L to 1 kg seed and sun dry before storage
Restrictions: When using a pesticide or botanical, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label
Do not use chemicals with the same mode of action year after year as this can lead to resistance, always consult the most recent list of registered pesticides of
Disinfect storage facility and bags with pirimiphos- methyl product (e.g.
II); Following disinfection wait 6 hours before entry; Maximum 2 applications per 6 months.
Use one tablet per 25 kg storage bag.
WHO - Fumigant, Very toxic if swallowed or inhaled; Following fumigation, wait 6 months before consumption or sale.
